name: Talking/vocal formant voice from a resonant filter into sample-rate reduction (sweet-spot aliasing formants)
goal: Create a talking, vowel-like voice without a formant filter: send a harmonically rich oscillator through a filter with healthy resonance and then a sample-rate reducer, find the sweet spots where aliasing creates formants, then animate it with a tempo-synced LFO on cutoff whose rate multiplier is stepped by a sequencer plus slow random modulation of the reduction amount, and send only content above ~1.5 kHz to a delay — a formant-voice delta that differs from formant-filter / spectral-vocode skills.

source.title: Creating a vocal formant speaking voice in VCV Rack

prerequisites: Oscillator with rich harmonics (saw/pulse), resonant filter, bit-crusher/sample-rate-reduction (decimator)
Clock-synced LFO, step sequencer for modulation values, slow random source, delay and a crossover/HP split
constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Web Audio note (implementation, not from transcript): sample-rate reduction = AudioWorklet sample-and-hold decimator; keep it after the filter.
Distinct from cinematic-formant-comb-pad-phaser-fx and spectral-warp-vocode-formant-stretch-smear (no formant filter or spectral warp).

steps.action: Patch a harmonically rich oscillator into a filter and add a healthy amount of resonance.
Send the filter output into a sample-rate reduction stage (bit-crusher with sample-rate reduction) after the filter.
Slowly sweep the sample-rate reduction amount (and cutoff) to find the sweet spots where formants appear and the sound starts to 'talk'.
In a patch: sequence the rich oscillator, modulate the filter cutoff with a tempo-synced LFO, and use a step sequencer to change the LFO's rate multiplication per step.
Slowly and randomly modulate the sample-rate reduction amount for different timbres; bring the reducer's wet signal up gradually.
steps.expect: Shifting formants and timbres over time

steps.action: Send only the high frequencies (around 1500 Hz and above) through a delay as an extra layer.
steps.expect: Airy delayed formant highs without muddy lows

verification: Bypassing the sample-rate reducer removes the talking/formant character.
With stepped LFO multipliers the formant motion changes rate across the bar.
Delay returns contain only content above ~1.5 kHz.
